description: §8.10 Tier 2 loop hoisting × §19.8.3 (RUNTIME, sqlEngine:"real"): a HANDLED keyed read (`… !{ _ :> not }` / `!{ _ :> [] }`) NESTED in the loop body — inside an `if`, an `else`, a nested `if`, and a `.all()` inside an `if`. The loop is rewritten to one pre-fetch + a per-iteration Map lookup, and each read keeps its meaning: id 7 → the row, id 8 → `not` / `[]` (no row is not a failure), id 9 → the branch that does not read; when the pre-fetch fails to run (`gone` is declared but never created) each READ takes its arm. Pre-S455 the body rewrite did not reach a nested site: the read was emitted with no server boundary (`null /* client cannot evaluate */`), so every row read `not` on success, and the failing pre-fetch threw past the handler (the cells stayed "init").
rationale: §8.10: "A for-loop whose body contains a single keyed `?{}` read SHALL be rewritten to a single `WHERE IN (...)` pre-fetch plus per-iteration `Map` lookup." §8.10.3: "The rewritten loop is observationally equivalent to the un-rewritten loop". §19.8.3: a handled query's success value is the unhandled one's; only a query that fails to run reaches the arms.
